texture_import.importer_gotcha: Scripts/shuriken/ue_import_textures.py and Scripts/props/props_lib/ue_import_textures.py write their JSON next to the texture folder's PARENT by default, which would create a NEW file inside Exports/. Always set *_TEXTURE_OUT to a WorkFiles path. The props importer FAILS on unknown suffixes in a folder it scans, so new maps live in a Recolour/ subfolder, which neither importer's non-recursive glob reads.

math: n      = DetailBias + DetailScale * Detail                     (mean ~1: the multiple of the part's mean colour)
H      = log(AlbedoCeiling / max(cmax, 1e-4)) / log(HighlightRatio)   (the detail exponent the colour can afford)
C_hi   = min(DetailStrength, max(H, 0))                       (exponent for n > 1: highlights)
C_lo   = lerp(DetailStrength, C_hi, DarkFollow)                (exponent for n <= 1: the dark weave)
n'     = n <= 1 ? pow(n, C_lo) : pow(n, C_hi)
E(C)   = El(C_lo) + Eh(C_hi); El(c) = E[n^c ; n<=1] and Eh(c) = E[n^c ; n>1], each a CUBIC in c (MomentsLow / MomentsHigh = its 4 coefficients as RGBA) fitted exactly through c = 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5
MF_TintDetail.default_exactness: At the default Colour, H >= 1 for every part (gate G-H1), so C_hi = C_lo = 1, n' = n, and E(1) = DetailMean because the cubics pass exactly through c = 1. So Albedo = Colour * (DetailBias + DetailScale * Detail), which is the item contract.

MF_AlbedoRollOff.math: m = max channel; if m <= Knee: unchanged; else scale rgb by (Knee + (Limit-Knee)*(1-exp(-(m-Knee)/(Limit-Knee)))) / m. Keeps the hue and never exceeds Limit. With Knee >= Limit it is a hard min(rgb, Limit).

paper_defaults.why: paperbomb_art Palette.ceiling_linear = 0.962 is the art's own clip

MF_NormalStrength.math: N' = normalize(lerp(float3(0,0,1), N, Strength)); Strength 1 = unchanged

math: BaseColor = lerp(BaseColor, LetteringColour, Ink); Roughness = lerp(Roughness, LetteringRoughness, Ink)
MF_LetteringBand.source: References/Kunai/LETTERING_HOWTO.md section 5; Rect in UNREAL UV0 (V flipped by the FBX importer)

math: StoredScale(c, k) = sRGBdecode(k * sRGBencode(c)) per channel (exact piecewise sRGB)
SatGain(c, s, g)  = lerp(Y(c), c, s) * g
MF_InkDerive.note: The functions depend on parameters only, so UE can evaluate them as preshaders. The gains make them exact at the default colours, and they stay inside [0,1] for any colour.

new_maps.script: Scripts/unreal/materials/maps/make_kunai_wrap_detail.py (Blender headless, opens Assets/Shuriken.blend READ-ONLY, never saves)
new_maps.recipe: Bake M_Kunai_Wrap Base Color (Dye = 0) on SM_Kunai_Plain_LOD0 into a FLOAT image, exactly as kunai_wrap.bake_kunai does: B._alone(lod0), _absorber(steel material), _wrap_uv(lod0), B._bake_channel(..., 'Base Color', float image), spec.wrap_px 1024, then B._fill with B._coverage. Y = luminance(linear rgb). Ymean = mean over covered texels (fill texels carry the mean). Ylo/Yhi = min/max of Y. d = (Y - Ylo) / (Yhi - Ylo), written as 16-bit. Colour = mean linear rgb, Bias = Ylo / Ymean, Scale = (Yhi - Ylo) / Ymean.
gates: G-K1 bake parity: sRGB8(float bake) vs the shipped T_Kunai_Wrap_BC.png: max |diff| <= 1 level, mean <= 0.2 (bake-noise tolerance the kunai freeze used)
G-K2 default model vs shipped BC: dE00 mean <= 0.5, p99 <= 1.5

new_maps.recipe: d16 = round(65535 * sRGBdecode(T_SmokeBomb_Detail.R / 255)). This is a lossless re-encoding: every sRGB8 level maps to a distinct 16-bit value. The equality gate proves it.
gates: decode(d16) vs sRGBdecode(Detail8): max abs <= 1/65535 x 0.5
model(Detail16) vs BC: 0 stored levels (as the shipped Detail)

new_maps.script: Scripts/unreal/materials/maps/make_paperbomb_recolour_maps.py (Blender headless; imports props_lib READ-ONLY and monkeypatches nothing on disk)
new_maps.recipe: see MATERIAL_PLAN.md 5.3: re-run bake.draw_art(spec, plan, seed=20260919, supersample=2) with paperbomb_art._composite and _downsample wrapped IN MEMORY to capture the 2x paper/red/black layers; build per-texel weights at 2x (W_P per channel = (clipped total - ink terms) / PaperColour; W_bw = a_b d_b K; W_bd = a_b (1-d_b) K; W_rw = (1-a_b) a_r d_r (1-p_r) K; W_rd = (1-a_b) a_r (1-d_r)(1-p_r) K; W_rp = (1-a_b) a_r p_r K); box-downsample 2:1 with paperbomb_art._down; compose into the atlas with atlas.compose (back face: W_P = back.base_colour / PaperColour, inks 0; rim: rim_gradient / PaperColour). RGB = W_P / PaperWeightScale, A = W_rp

V2_ue_uvplane_basecolor.what: UE: engine Plane, orthographic SceneCapture2D at the texture's resolution, capture_source SCS_BASE_COLOR, RTF_RGBA32F, exported as EXR. The GBuffer stores base colour as 8-bit sRGB, so captures are quantised to 1 level
V2_ue_uvplane_basecolor.gate: default MI vs twin: |diff| <= 1 sRGB level at p99.9, mean <= 0.3 level; BC-direct MI vs PNG: reported (BC1 error), not gated
V2_ue_uvplane_basecolor.calibration: first capture the BC-direct instance and find the UV orientation (flip/rotation) by cross-correlating with the PNG

gates: clip: <= 0.1 % of covered texels with any channel >= 0.949
banding: in the 8-bit sRGB output, dominant channel inside its p1..p99 range: largest gap between consecutive occupied levels <= 3 AND occupied levels >= 0.5 x (p99 - p1 level span)

detail kept: std(log L_recolour) >= 0.25 x std(log L_default) (twin); Spearman rank corr(L_recolour, L_default) >= 0.98 on the UE 8-bit captures (the twin mapping is monotone, so on floats it is 1 by construction)
mean: dE00(part mean albedo, Colour x Detail Mean) <= 3 for colours whose max channel <= 0.85 (above that the roll-off takes over by design)
